section_1.title: Introduction: Beyond the Static Slope
section_1.content: Transition from the static 'rise over run' slope formula to the dynamic concept of 'instantaneous sensitivity'. Introduce the idea that a derivative is an operator that transforms a function of position into a function of change.
section_1.example: A cheetah chasing a gazelle: The average speed is the stretch of the chase, while the derivative is the cheetah's exact speedometer reading at a specific millisecond.

section_2.title: The Visual Mechanism: The Shrinking Secant
section_2.content: Use a graphical animation: Show a secant line connecting two points on a curve. As the distance between points (Δx) approaches zero, the secant line visually 'snaps' into the tangent line. This transformation represents the limit process.
section_2.example: A camera lens zooming in on a curved roller coaster track until the track looks like a perfectly straight line segment.

section_3.title: Derivative as a Transformation Map
section_3.content: Explain the derivative as a function-to-function machine (f → f'). If the input function describes a state (position), the output function describes the behavior of that state (velocity).
section_3.example: A smart thermostat: If the input is 'Room Temperature over time', the derivative output is 'How fast the room is heating up or cooling down', allowing the system to react before it gets too hot.

section_4.title: Geometric Interpretation: The Slope Field
section_4.content: Visualize the derivative as a 'direction field'. Instead of a single number, see the derivative as a map of arrows across the coordinate plane, indicating the 'flow' of the function at every point.
section_4.example: Visualizing ocean currents: The surface of the water is the function, and the derivative is the map of tiny arrows showing exactly which way a toy boat would drift at any given coordinate.

section_5.title: Summary & Synthesis
section_5.content: Recap: The derivative is not just a calculation, but a transformation that reveals the 'DNA of change' inherent in any system. Preparing students for the reverse process: Integration.
section_5.example: Summarizing the journey: We went from calculating a single 'slope' to understanding the 'flow' of an entire system—essential for physics, economics, and AI optimization.

section_4.example: Visualizing ocean currents: The surface of the water is the function, and the derivative is the map of tiny arrows showing exactly which way a toy boat would drift at any given coordinate.

section_5.title: Summary & Synthesis
section_5.content: Recap: The derivative is not just a calculation, but a transformation that reveals the 'DNA of change' inherent in any system. Preparing students for the reverse process: Integration.
section_5.example: Summarizing the journey: We went from calculating a single 'slope' to understanding the 'flow' of an entire system—essential for physics, economics, and AI optimization.

section_1.title: Introduction: Beyond the Static Slope
lecture_lines: Derivatives measure dynamic change, not static slopes.
Average speed hides the cheetah's instant velocity.
Watch the speedometer at one exact millisecond.
Derivatives capture this instantaneous sensitivity perfectly.
Position data transforms into vital movement insights.

section_2.title: The Visual Mechanism: The Shrinking Secant
lecture_lines: A secant connects two points on the curve.
Zoom in as the distance shrinks toward zero.
The line tilts, tracking the roller coaster.
It snaps perfectly into the tangent line.
This limit defines the instantaneous derivative.

section_3.title: Derivative as a Transformation Map
lecture_lines: Derivatives act as a function-to-function machine.
Input temperature; output the rate of change.
It reveals how fast the room heats.

section_4.title: Geometric Interpretation: The Slope Field
lecture_lines: Visualize derivatives as a field of arrows.
Each arrow shows flow at that coordinate.
Ocean currents map the function's directionality.

section_5.title: Summary & Synthesis
lecture_lines: Derivatives reveal the DNA of dynamic change.
We transformed static slopes into system flow.
Now, we are prepared for reverse integration.
